questions.prompt: How should you read the flag `-p 8080:80`?

options.text: container port 8080 maps to host port 80
host port 8080 maps to container port 80
both ports must always be identical
it blocks port 8080 on the host

questions.explanation: The format is host:container. -p 8080:80 forwards traffic from port 8080 on your machine to port 80 inside the container.

questions.prompt: Which command opens an interactive shell inside a running container named web?
questions.explanation: docker exec runs a new command inside a running container; -it makes it interactive with a terminal. docker run would create a new container instead.

questions.prompt: Why is docker exec usually preferred over docker attach for debugging?

options.text: exec starts a separate process, so leaving it does not stop the container, while attach connects to the main process where Ctrl+C can stop it
attach cannot open a shell at all

questions.explanation: exec launches a new process (like a shell); exiting it leaves the container running. attach connects to the main process, so Ctrl+C can terminate the whole container.

questions.prompt: To stream a container's output live, run docker ______ -f <container>. (one word)
questions.explanation: docker logs -f follows the container's output, streaming new lines until you stop it with Ctrl+C.

questions.prompt: Which statements about stopping and removing containers are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: docker stop asks the process to shut down gracefully before forcing it
docker rm removes a stopped container
docker rm -f can remove a running container
--rm keeps the container forever after it exits

questions.explanation: stop is graceful, rm removes a stopped container, and rm -f forces removal of a running one. --rm does the opposite of (d): it auto-removes the container on exit.

questions.prompt: Order these commands to run, inspect, and clean up a web server.
questions.explanation: Start the container, read its logs, step inside to look around, then force-remove it when you are done.
